record.field:
When a document is delivered to you through a secure link, the file is placed on encrypted storage and the link that leads to it expires on a date set in advance. Your email address is used to send you this link and to record who downloaded what, and when.

Once the expiry date has passed, the file is deleted from the storage. The access log and the transfer record are kept without the content, because they are the proof of what was delivered.

Section 23 of the Quebec private sector privacy act: personal information is destroyed once the purpose for which it was collected or used has been achieved. Here, the purpose is delivering the file to its recipient.

The actual period is the transfer's expiry date, chosen when sending and capped by the brand's "Maximum retention". The `_cron_purge_expired` job deletes the object storage files of expired transfers, and `_cron_gc_drafts` collects abandoned drafts. This bridge destroys nothing itself: it records in the register what these jobs have just done.
Files uploaded by the sender (unclassified content), recipients' email addresses, access log (timestamp, IP address, user agent).
Period set to 0 days: destruction follows each transfer's own expiry date, not a fixed delay. The value is there so that the purpose has a policy attached, not to trigger a purge.
